elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨登革病毒型2(DENV2)株系,如QML-22,的基因型差异是否与抗原差异相关。这是重要的,因为了解抗原变异可以为抗病毒药物开发和疫苗接种策略提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用非人类灵长类动物感染产生的抗血清来表征QML-22的抗原特征。研究重点是DENV2及其与其他DENV血清型的关系。
elements_zh.methods: 使用非人类灵长类动物感染QML-22或DENV2参考株S16803所产生的抗血清来评估中和能力。测试了针对包膜蛋白域I特定表位的3F9抗体对QML-22和其他DENV2株系的中和能力。进行了进化分析,比较不同株系中该表位的序列。
elements_zh.main_results: QML-22并未被针对地方性DENV2毒株的抗血清有效中和,但被DENV1、3和4感染产生的抗血清更好地中和。QML-22中的3F9表位与所有DENV2毒株的可能共同祖先相比显示出独特的氨基酸。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明QML-22的抗原差异具有显著性,并可能与其独特的中和表型有关。这突显了DENV2的抗原多样化,并提出了新血清型进化的可能性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为DENV2的抗原变异提供了见解,这可能有助于开发更有效的抗病毒药物,并改进针对新兴株系的疫苗接种策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于摘要证据,这可能限制分析的深度。然而,研究结果得到了直接实验数据和进化比较的支持,提供了中等程度的置信度。

papers.abstract_zh: 登革病毒 1-4(DENV1-4)主要在人类和Aedes蚊虫的流行循环中传播。然而,罕见的登革热暴发来源于非人类灵长类动物。这些跨物种溢出是由森林病毒基因型引起的,这些基因型与同型的流行株密切相关,但有些是由在系统发育树上位于四个经典型之间的株系引起的。尚不清楚这些基因型差异是否反映在相应的抗原差异上。在这里,我们表征了QML-22的抗原特征,QML-22是一种与DENV2最接近的变异株。在抗原图谱上,QML-22与其他全球代表性DENV2株系聚类在一起。QML-22对针对流行DENV2的抗血清中和能力不如其他DENV2株系,但对DENV1、DENV3和DENV4感染产生的抗血清中和能力优于其他DENV2株系。QML-22在包膜(E)蛋白的域I中有一簇独特的氨基酸残基,而在E蛋白的其他区域仅有零星的点突变。一种针对E蛋白域I特定表位的强效中和抗DENV2抗体3F9,对QML-22的中和能力比其他流行DENV2株系低1000倍以上,而其他交叉反应性和DENV2特异性抗体对QML-22和流行株的中和能力相似。当用非人类灵长类动物感染QML-22或DENV2参考株S16803的抗血清去除异源病毒颗粒后,同源中和能力未受影响,但异源中和能力降低,这表明同源中和是由不同的表位引起的。进化分析显示,3F9表位相较于其他中和表位处于较弱的正选择压力下,并且QML-22在该表位上具有与所有DENV2可能共同祖先不同的独特氨基酸。这些发现为登革病毒(DENV)的抗原多样化提供了见解,并提出了新血清型出现的可能性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨登革病毒型2(DENV2)株系,如QML-22,的基因型差异是否与抗原差异相关。这是重要的,因为了解抗原变异可以为抗病毒药物开发和疫苗接种策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用非人类灵长类动物感染产生的抗血清来表征QML-22的抗原特征。研究重点是DENV2及其与其他DENV血清型的关系。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用非人类灵长类动物感染QML-22或DENV2参考株S16803所产生的抗血清来评估中和能力。测试了针对包膜蛋白域I特定表位的3F9抗体对QML-22和其他DENV2株系的中和能力。进行了进化分析,比较不同株系中该表位的序列。
analysis_zh.main_results: QML-22并未被针对地方性DENV2毒株的抗血清有效中和,但被DENV1、3和4感染产生的抗血清更好地中和。QML-22中的3F9表位与所有DENV2毒株的可能共同祖先相比显示出独特的氨基酸。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明QML-22的抗原差异具有显著性,并可能与其独特的中和表型有关。这突显了DENV2的抗原多样化,并提出了新血清型进化的可能性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为DENV2的抗原变异提供了见解,这可能有助于开发更有效的抗病毒药物,并改进针对新兴株系的疫苗接种策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于摘要证据,这可能限制分析的深度。然而,研究结果得到了直接实验数据和进化比较的支持,提供了中等程度的置信度。

papers.title: Tetravalent dengue mRNA vaccination orchestrates balanced four-serotype immunity with durable memory and protection in mice.
papers.abstract: An effective dengue vaccine must establish durable immunity across four dengue virus (DENV) serotypes, evade antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), and overcome immune imprinting from prior exposure. Here, we developed TetprM-E mRNA-LNP, a tetravalent vaccine comprising LNP-formulated nucleoside-modified mRNAs encoding DENV1-4 precursor membrane-envelope (prM-E) antigens, and evaluated its immunogenicity, durability, protection and breath across serotype-specific immune backgrounds. Three immunization strategies elicited neutralizing titers greater than 1:1500 against each serotype. Passive transfer of immune sera conferred 100% survival and reduced viremia after lethal DENV2 challenge in immunocompromised mice. Vaccination induced DENV envelope (env)-specific CD8+T cells and CD4-dependent germinal-center responses. DENV env-binding antibodies persisted for 34 weeks alongside DENV env-specific memory B cells. Vaccine-elicited sera showed no measurable in vitro ADE. Although monovalent priming initially biased antibody responses, TetprM-E mRNA-LNP vaccination broadened neutralization across DENV1-4 regardless of priming serotype. Together, TetprM-E mRNA-LNP elicits broad, durable, and protective immunity despite serologic constraints from pre-existing immunity.

The researchers created TetprM-E mRNA-LNP, a vaccine encoding DENV1-4 prM-E antigens, and evaluated its immunogenicity and protective capacity in mice. The vaccine induced high neutralizing titers against all serotypes and conferred complete survival and reduced viremia in immunocompromised mice after DENV2 challenge. papers.abstract_zh: 一种有效的登革病毒疫苗必须在四种登革病毒(DENV)血清型中建立持久的免疫力,避免抗体依赖性增强(ADE),并克服先前暴露引起的免疫印记。在这里,我们开发了TetprM-E mRNA-LNP,一种包含针对DENV1-4的前膜-包膜(prM-E)抗原的四价疫苗,其通过脂质纳米颗粒(LNP)递送的核苷修饰mRNA进行制备,并评估了其在特定血清型免疫背景下的免疫原性、持久性、保护性和广谱性。三种免疫策略均诱导了针对每种血清型的中和抗体滴度大于1:1500。将免疫血清被动转移至免疫缺陷小鼠后,可实现100%存活率,并在致命性DENV2感染后降低病毒血症。疫苗接种诱导了针对登革病毒包膜(env)的CD8+T细胞和依赖CD4的生发中心反应。登革病毒env结合抗体与env特异性记忆B细胞在34周内持续存在。由疫苗诱导的血清在体外未检测到可测量的ADE。尽管单价免疫最初偏向抗体应答,但TetprM-E mRNA-LNP 疫苗接种无论先前免疫血清型如何,均能广谱中和DENV1-4。综上所述,TetprM-E mRNA-LNP能够在存在先前免疫血清学限制的情况下,诱导广泛、持久且具有保护性的免疫力。

papers.title: MicroRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases: from biomarker discovery to clinical implementation.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are increasingly investigated as host-response biomarkers for infectious diseases, but translation from differential-expression studies to clinically deployable diagnostics remains limited. AREAS COVERED: This review evaluates the diagnostic and translational potential of miRNAs across malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Zika virus infection, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Japanese encephalitis and Nipah virus disease. Unlike prior reviews focused mainly on biomarker discovery or detection technologies, it provides a cross-disease translational perspective linking miRNA signatures with analytical and clinical validation, point-of-care development, clinical implementation, economic considerations and deployment in resource-limited settings. EXPERT OPINION: The next phase of miRNA diagnostics should prioritize reproducible multi-miRNA signatures, standardized pre-analytical workflows and prospective multicentre validation rather than continued biomarker discovery alone. Clinical adoption will depend on integrating these signatures into affordable sample-to-answer platforms and demonstrating that results improve defined clinical decisions under real-world conditions.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the use of microRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for dengue virus and dengue disease, including severe dengue, dengue hemorrhagic fever, dengue shock syndrome, dengue fever, and dengue virus 1–4. The central question is how miRNA signatures can be translated into clinically deployable diagnostics for these conditions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review evaluates the diagnostic and translational potential of miRNAs across dengue virus and related diseases. It provides a cross-disease translational perspective, linking miRNA signatures with analytical and clinical validation, point-of-care development, clinical implementation, economic considerations, and deployment in resource-limited settings. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that miRNA-based diagnostics have potential for clinical implementation in dengue disease, particularly when integrated into affordable sample-to-answer platforms. It emphasizes the need for reproducible multi-miRNA signatures and standardized pre-analytical workflows to improve clinical utility.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is a lack of standardized pre-analytical workflows and prospective multicentre validation for miRNA-based diagnostics in dengue. The review also notes that continued biomarker discovery alone is insufficient for clinical deployment, and real-world conditions must be considered to demonstrate improved clinical decisions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize the development of reproducible multi-miRNA signatures, standardized pre-analytical workflows, and prospective multicentre validation for miRNA-based diagnostics in dengue. These efforts are critical for translating miRNA research into practical, affordable point-of-care solutions.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of microRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for dengue virus and dengue disease, including severe dengue, dengue hemorrhagic fever, dengue shock syndrome, dengue fever, and dengue virus 1–4. It evaluates the translational potential of miRNA signatures, emphasizing the need for integration into affordable platforms and validation under real-world conditions. The review highlights that while miRNA research is promising, there are gaps in standardization and multicentre validation. It suggests that future efforts should focus on developing reproducible multi-miRNA signatures and improving pre-analytical workflows to enhance clinical utility. The review also notes that continued biomarker discovery alone is not sufficient for clinical deployment.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于基于微小RNA的现场快速诊断方法在登革热和相关疾病中的应用,包括登革热轻症、登革热出血热、登革热休克综合征、登革热重症以及登革热1–4型。核心问题是:如何将miRNA特征转化为这些疾病的可临床部署诊断方法。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述评估了miRNA在登革热及相关疾病中的诊断和转化潜力。它提供了一个跨疾病转化视角,将miRNA特征与分析和临床验证、现场快速诊断开发、临床应用、经济考量以及资源有限地区的部署联系起来。综述中并未明确报告元分析或汇总估计。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述强调,基于miRNA的诊断方法在登革热疾病中具有临床应用的潜力,特别是在整合到经济实惠的样本到答案平台后。它指出需要可重复的多miRNA特征和标准化的预分析流程以提高临床实用性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 目前缺乏基于miRNA的登革热诊断方法的标准化预分析流程和前瞻性多中心验证。综述还指出,仅继续发现生物标志物不足以实现临床部署,必须考虑真实世界条件以证明其对临床决策的改善。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先发展基于miRNA的登革热诊断方法的可重复多miRNA特征、标准化预分析流程以及前瞻性多中心验证。这些努力对于将miRNA研究转化为实际、经济的现场快速诊断解决方案至关重要。

papers.abstract_zh: 引言:微小RNA(miRNA)作为感染性疾病的免疫应答生物标志物正受到越来越多的关注,但将差异表达研究转化为可临床部署的诊断方法仍存在局限。研究领域:本综述评估了miRNA在疟疾、登革热、基孔肯雅热、寨卡病毒感染、克里米亚-刚果出血热、日本脑炎和尼帕病毒感染等疾病中的诊断和转化潜力。与以往主要关注生物标志物发现或检测技术的综述不同,本综述提供了一个跨疾病转化视角,将miRNA特征与分析和临床验证、现场快速诊断开发、临床应用、经济考量以及资源有限地区的部署联系起来。专家观点:miRNA诊断的下一步应优先考虑可重复的多miRNA特征、标准化的预分析流程以及前瞻性多中心验证,而不是仅仅继续进行生物标志物的发现。临床采用将取决于将这些特征整合到经济实惠的样本到答案平台中,并在真实世界条件下证明其结果能够改善特定的临床决策。

papers.title: Etiological spectrum of acute encephalitis syndrome in children in India: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) continues to be an important cause of illness and death among children in India. While Japanese encephalitis (JE) virus has traditionally been regarded as the leading cause, recent studies indicate that the range of causative organisms has widened considerably. AIM: To estimate the pooled proportion of AES cases attributable to various common infectious etiologies among children aged 18 years or younger in India. METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Scopus was conducted for studies published between January 2000 and December 2025. Studies conducted in India that included at least 25 children (≤ 18 years) with AES and reported laboratory-confirmed etiologies were considered eligible. Case reports and small case series were excluded. Quality assessment of included studies was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. A random-effects model was used to obtain pooled estimates and their corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: A total of 69 studies were included in the final analysis. Scrub typhus emerged as the most common cause, accounting for 20% (95%CI: 13%-27%) of AES cases, followed by JE at 13% (95%CI: 11%-15%). Enterovirus accounted for 6% of the cases (95%CI: 3%-9%). Dengue, herpes simplex virus and Epstein-Barr virus accounted for 5% of the cases each (95%CI: 3%-8%, 2%-9%, and 1%-11%, respectively). Mumps and chikungunya virus accounted for 4% each (95%CI: 1%-8%, and 2%-5%, respectively). CONCLUSION: Scrub typhus and JE are the leading identifiable etiology of pediatric AES in India. Broader diagnostic methods, including molecular techniques, may improve the diagnostic yield and facilitate early targeted therapy in children with AES.

papers.title: Immature Platelet Fraction in Viral Infections: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Background: Reticulated platelets, reported by modern hematology analyzers as the immature platelet fraction (IPF%) or the absolute immature platelet count (IPC), index thrombopoiesis and have been proposed as biomarkers in the thrombocytopenia of viral infection. Methods: This systematic review, conducted and reported following PRISMA 2020 and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261501412), examined how these parameters have been used across viral diseases. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2000 to May 2025 for observational studies of adults with viral infection reporting IPF, IPC, or reticulated platelets, and methodological robustness was appraised with the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Results: Twenty-two studies were included and synthesized narratively. Applications differed by pathogen: in dengue, serial IPF increases consistently preceded platelet recovery, although proposed thresholds varied; in COVID-19, higher immature platelet parameters were associated with severity and mortality but were inconsistent after adjustment. Evidence in chronic hepatitis, HIV, hantavirus, and Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever was mainly pathophysiological, and data in critically ill patients were almost confined to COVID-19. Conclusions: Clinical value appears disease- and outcome-specific: serial IPF best predicts platelet recovery in dengue, whereas prognostic use in COVID-19 remains insufficiently validated. Analytical heterogeneity and the absence of transferable thresholds currently limit clinical implementation.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on dengue virus and its associated disease, specifically examining the role of the immature platelet fraction (IPF%) and absolute immature platelet count (IPC) as biomarkers in thrombocytopenia during viral infections. The central question is how these parameters are used across different dengue-related conditions and their clinical relevance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261501412). It searched PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from January 2000 to May 2025 for observational studies of adults with viral infections, specifically those reporting IPF, IPC, or reticulated platelets. Methodological robustness was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review synthesized 22 studies narratively. It found that in dengue, serial increases in IPF consistently preceded platelet recovery, although proposed thresholds varied. In contrast, higher immature platelet parameters in COVID-19 were associated with severity and mortality but were inconsistent after adjustment. The clinical value of these parameters appears to be disease- and outcome-specific.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Analytical heterogeneity and the absence of transferable thresholds currently limit the clinical implementation of IPF and IPC as biomarkers. Evidence in chronic hepatitis, HIV, hantavirus, and Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever was mainly pathophysiological, and data in critically ill patients were almost confined to COVID-19.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to establish consistent thresholds for IPF and IPC across different viral infections, particularly for dengue. There is a need for more robust studies to validate the prognostic use of these parameters in dengue and other related conditions.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review explores the use of immature platelet fraction (IPF%) and absolute immature platelet count (IPC) as biomarkers in thrombocytopenia associated with dengue virus infections. The review, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, analyzed 22 observational studies from 2000 to 2025, focusing on adults with dengue-related conditions. It found that in dengue, serial IPF increases consistently preceded platelet recovery, though thresholds varied. In contrast, higher immature platelet parameters in COVID-19 were linked to severity and mortality but were inconsistent after adjustment. The clinical utility of these parameters appears to be disease-specific, with limited transferability across conditions. The review highlights the need for further research to standardize thresholds and validate their prognostic value in dengue and related viral infections.

papers.title_zh: 病毒性感染中未成熟血小板分数:当前应用与未来展望的系统综述
papers.source_body_en: Background: Reticulated platelets, reported by modern hematology analyzers as the immature platelet fraction (IPF%) or the absolute immature platelet count (IPC), index thrombopoiesis and have been proposed as biomarkers in the thrombocytopenia of viral infection. Methods: This systematic review, conducted and reported following PRISMA 2020 and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261501412), examined how these parameters have been used across viral diseases. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2000 to May 2025 for observational studies of adults with viral infection reporting IPF, IPC, or reticulated platelets, and methodological robustness was appraised with the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Results: Twenty-two studies were included and synthesized narratively. Applications differed by pathogen: in dengue, serial IPF increases consistently preceded platelet recovery, although proposed thresholds varied; in COVID-19, higher immature platelet parameters were associated with severity and mortality but were inconsistent after adjustment. Evidence in chronic hepatitis, HIV, hantavirus, and Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever was mainly pathophysiological, and data in critically ill patients were almost confined to COVID-19. Conclusions: Clinical value appears disease- and outcome-specific: serial IPF best predicts platelet recovery in dengue, whereas prognostic use in COVID-19 remains insufficiently validated. Analytical heterogeneity and the absence of transferable thresholds currently limit clinical implementation.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:现代血液分析仪将网织血小板报告为未成熟血小板分数(IPF%)或绝对未成熟血小板计数(IPC),这些参数可作为血小板生成的指标,并被提出作为病毒性感染血小板减少症的生物标志物。方法:本系统综述遵循PRISMA 2020指南进行,并在PROSPERO(CRD420261501412)注册。通过检索PubMed、Scopus和Cochrane Library(时间范围为2000年1月至2025年5月),评估了这些参数在不同病毒性疾病中的应用情况。对成人病毒性感染的观察性研究进行了系统分析,并采用Newcastle–Ottawa量表评估方法学的稳健性。结果:共纳入22项研究并进行叙述性综合。应用情况因病原体而异:在登革热中,连续IPF升高始终先于血小板恢复,尽管提出的阈值有所不同;在COVID-19中,较高的未成熟血小板参数与严重程度和死亡率相关,但在调整后结果不一致。慢性肝炎、HIV、汉坦病毒和克里米亚–刚果出血热的证据主要基于发病机制,而危重患者的数据几乎仅限于COVID-19。结论:临床价值似乎具有疾病和预后特异性:在登革热中,连续IPF最能预测血小板恢复,而在COVID-19中,其预后用途仍缺乏充分验证。分析的异质性和缺乏可转移的阈值目前限制了其临床应用。

papers.title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.
papers.abstract: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. papers.title: Near or Far?
papers.abstract: Dengue fever is a growing public health threat in urban Bangladesh, yet the role of hospital proximity as a spatial determinant of case detection remains largely untested. This chapter examines whether residents living closer to a dengue-treating hospital are more likely to be detected as cases, using cross-sectional survey data from two Dhaka sites: Dhaka Community Medical College Hospital (Boro Moghbazar) and Mugdha Medical College Hospital. Detection declined significantly with distance, and the effect persisted after adjustment for awareness, age, and prior infection, with each additional 100 meters of distance lowering the odds of detection by roughly 5%. Having an affected neighbor was the strongest correlate of detection, indicating fine-scale spatial clustering. Healthcare-worker responses revealed high knowledge but lower preventive practice, suggesting an institutional engagement gap. A divergent pattern in one distant zone coincided with localized drainage construction, suggesting environmental disturbances can temporarily override the proximity effect.
papers.journal: Mitigation Measures for Environmental and Humanitarian Disasters

papers.title_zh: 近还是远?
papers.source_body_en: Dengue fever is a growing public health threat in urban Bangladesh, yet the role of hospital proximity as a spatial determinant of case detection remains largely untested. This chapter examines whether residents living closer to a dengue-treating hospital are more likely to be detected as cases, using cross-sectional survey data from two Dhaka sites: Dhaka Community Medical College Hospital (Boro Moghbazar) and Mugdha Medical College Hospital. Detection declined significantly with distance, and the effect persisted after adjustment for awareness, age, and prior infection, with each additional 100 meters of distance lowering the odds of detection by roughly 5%. Having an affected neighbor was the strongest correlate of detection, indicating fine-scale spatial clustering. Healthcare-worker responses revealed high knowledge but lower preventive practice, suggesting an institutional engagement gap. A divergent pattern in one distant zone coincided with localized drainage construction, suggesting environmental disturbances can temporarily override the proximity effect.
papers.abstract_zh: 登革热在孟加拉国的城市地区正成为一个日益严重的公共卫生威胁,但医院距离作为病例检测空间决定因素的作用仍 largely 未经检验。本章利用来自达卡两个地点的横断面调查数据,探讨居住在距离登革热治疗医院更近的居民是否更有可能被检测为病例:达卡社区医学学院医院(Boro Moghbazar)和 Mugdha 医学院医院。检测率随距离显著下降,且在调整了意识、年龄和既往感染后,这一效应依然存在,每增加 100 米的距离,病例检测的几率大致降低 5%。拥有受影响邻居是检测率最强的关联因素,表明存在细粒度的空间聚集现象。医疗工作者的回应显示了较高的知识水平但较低的预防实践,这表明存在机构参与的差距。在一个偏远区域中出现的相反模式与局部排水工程的建设相吻合,这表明环境扰动可能暂时掩盖距离效应。

papers.title: Pemberdayaan Masyarakat dengan Gerakan Pemberantasan Sarang Nyamuk (PSN) dan Survey Vektor DBD
papers.abstract: This community service activity aimed to improve students’ knowledge and awareness of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) prevention through the Mosquito Nest Eradication Movement (PSN), vector surveys, epidemiological investigations, and early detection of DHF. The activity was conducted on August 29–30, 2026, at SMA Negeri 4 Manado, involving 60 students in collaboration with healthcare workers, Ranomut Community Health Center, the Manado City Health Office, and school representatives. The implementation methods included preparation, health education, vector surveys, follow-up actions, and evaluation. The educational materials covered the 3M Plus approach, identification of mosquito breeding sites, dengue transmission prevention, epidemiological investigations, and recognition of DHF symptoms and warning signs. The results showed that PSN education and vector surveys were conducted according to the planned topics. The survey found no mosquito larvae in potential breeding sites within the school environment, which was attributed to the dry season. This activity is expected to encourage students and school personnel to actively maintain environmental cleanliness and implement PSN measures sustainably.

papers.abstract_zh: 本次社区服务活动旨在通过灭蚊运动(PSN)、媒介调查、流行病学调查和登革热出血热(DHF)的早期检测,提高学生对登革热出血热(DHF)预防的知识和意识。活动于2026年8月29日至30日在万隆第四国立中学(SMA Negeri 4 Manado)进行,涉及60名学生,与医疗工作者、拉诺穆特社区卫生中心(Ranomut Community Health Center)、万隆市卫生办公室(Manado City Health Office)及学校代表合作开展。实施方法包括准备阶段、健康教育、媒介调查、后续行动和评估。教育材料涵盖3M Plus方法、蚊虫孳生地识别、登革热传播预防、流行病学调查以及登革热出血热症状和警示信号的识别。结果显示,PSN教育和媒介调查均按照计划主题进行。调查发现学校环境中潜在孳生地内没有蚊虫幼虫,这归因于旱季。本次活动预计能够鼓励学生和学校工作人员积极维护环境卫生,并可持续实施PSN措施。

papers.title: Pengaruh ekstrak rimpang temulawak (Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb) terhadap mortalitas larva Aedes albopictus
papers.abstract: Background: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) is caused by the dengue virus (DENV), transmitted through of Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Larval control is essential to break transmission. One environmentally friendly alternative is natural larvicides. Temulawak rhizome (Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb) contains active compounds such as saponins, tanins, alkaloids, and flavonoids with potential as plant-based larvicides.Objectives: To evaluate the larvicidal effectiveness of Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb. rhizome extract against third-instar Aedes albopictus larvae.Methods: This study used a quantitative true experimental design with a post-test only control group. Samples were selected through purposive sampling. Temulawak rhizome extract was obtained through maceration using 96% ethanol. Larvae were tested at five concentrations (0.6%, 0.8%, 1.0%, 1.2%, and 1.5%) with observations at 3, 6, 12, and 24 hours. Data were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis test, Mann–Whitney post-hoc test, and probit analysis to determine LC50, LC90, LT50, and LT90. The preparation of Curcuma xanthorrhiza rhizome extract was conducted at the Biomedical Laboratory I, Faculty of Medicine, Universitas Palangka Raya, while larvicidal testing was performed at the Public Health Laboratory Center, Tanah Bumbu, South Kalimantan, Indonesia, from July to October 2025.Results: Larval mortality increased with higher concentrations and longer exposure. The Kruskal–Wallis test showed significant differences among treatments (p < 0.05). LC50 was 0.614% and LC90 was 1.459%, while LT50 was 5.613 hours and LT90 was 15.102 hours. Active metabolites are presumed to contribute to larval mortality.Conclusion: Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb. rhizome extract demonstrated effective larvicidal activity against third-instar Aedes albopictus larvae, with efficacy increasing according to extract concentration and exposure time. These findings provide scientific evidence supporting the potential use of C. xanthorrhiza as an environmentally friendly plant-based larvicide and contribute to the development of sustainable alternative strategies for dengue vector control.

Temulawak rhizome (Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb) contains active compounds such as saponins, tanins, alkaloids, and flavonoids with potential as plant-based larvicides.Objectives: To evaluate the larvicidal effectiveness of Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb. rhizome extract against third-instar Aedes albopictus larvae.Methods: This study used a quantitative true experimental design with a post-test only control group. Samples were selected through purposive sampling. Temulawak rhizome extract was obtained through maceration using 96% ethanol. Larvae were tested at five concentrations (0.6%, 0.8%, 1.0%, 1.2%, and 1.5%) with observations at 3, 6, 12, and 24 hours. Data were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis test, Mann–Whitney post-hoc test, and probit analysis to determine LC50, LC90, LT50, and LT90. The preparation of Curcuma xanthorrhiza rhizome extract was conducted at the Biomedical Laboratory I, Faculty of Medicine, Universitas Palangka Raya, while larvicidal testing was performed at the Public Health Laboratory Center, Tanah Bumbu, South Kalimantan, Indonesia, from July to October 2025.Results: Larval mortality increased with higher concentrations and longer exposure. The Kruskal–Wallis test showed significant differences among treatments (p < 0.05). LC50 was 0.614% and LC90 was 1.459%, while LT50 was 5.613 hours and LT90 was 15.102 hours. Active metabolites are presumed to contribute to larval mortality.Conclusion: Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb. rhizome extract demonstrated effective larvicidal activity against third-instar Aedes albopictus larvae, with efficacy increasing according to extract concentration and exposure time. These findings provide scientific evidence supporting the potential use of C. xanthorrhiza as an environmentally friendly plant-based larvicide and contribute to the development of sustainable alternative strategies for dengue vector control.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the larvicidal effectiveness of Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb extract against third-instar Aedes albopictus larvae. The research is motivated by the need for environmentally friendly alternatives to control dengue transmission, as Aedes albopictus is a key vector for dengue disease. The study employed a quantitative true experimental design with a post-test only control group, using purposive sampling. Temulawak rhizome extract was prepared via maceration with 96% ethanol and tested at five concentrations over specific exposure times. The results showed that larval mortality increased with higher concentrations and longer exposure, with significant differences among treatments (p < 0.05). The LC50 and LC90 values were 0.614% and 1.459%, respectively, while LT50 and LT90 were 5.613 hours and 15.102 hours. The findings suggest that the extract could be a viable, eco-friendly larvicide for dengue vector control. The study provides scientific evidence for the potential use of C. xanthorrhiza in this context, though no limitations are explicitly reported.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热出血热(DHF)是由登革病毒(DENV)引起的,通过埃及伊蚊和白纹伊蚊传播。控制幼虫是打破传播链的关键。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用定量真实实验设计,仅进行后测控制组。样本通过目的抽样法选取。姜黄根提取物的制备在帕朗卡拉大学医学院生物医学实验室I进行,而幼虫杀灭测试则在南加里曼丹省坦布布县公共卫生实验室中心进行,时间为2025年7月至10月。
elements_zh.methods: 姜黄根提取物通过96%乙醇浸渍法获得。幼虫在五个浓度(0.6%、0.8%、1.0%、1.2%和1.5%)下进行测试,观察时间为3、6、12和24小时。数据通过Kruskal–Wallis检验、Mann–Whitney事后检验和Probit分析进行分析,以确定LC50、LC90、LT50和LT90。
elements_zh.main_results: 幼虫死亡率随着浓度的增加和暴露时间的延长而增加。Kruskal–Wallis检验显示不同浓度之间存在显著差异(p < 0.05)。LC50为0.614%,LC90为1.459%,而LT50为5.613小时,LT90为15.102小时。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 姜黄根提取物对白纹伊蚊三龄幼虫表现出有效的幼虫杀灭活性,其效果随着提取物浓度和暴露时间的增加而增强。这些发现为姜黄根作为环保型植物源幼虫杀灭剂的潜在应用提供了科学依据。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现有助于开发可持续的登革热控制替代策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据未报告局限性。研究设计为定量真实实验设计,仅进行后测控制组,结果基于对幼虫死亡率的统计分析。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:登革热出血热(DHF)是由登革病毒(DENV)引起的,通过埃及伊蚊和白纹伊蚊传播。控制幼虫是打破传播链的关键。一种环保的替代方法是天然幼虫杀灭剂。姜黄根(Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb)含有皂苷、单宁、生物碱和黄酮类等活性化合物,具有作为植物源幼虫杀灭剂的潜力。目的:评估姜黄根提取物对白纹伊蚊三龄幼虫的幼虫杀灭效果。方法:本研究采用定量真实实验设计,仅进行后测控制组。样本通过目的抽样法选取。姜黄根提取物通过96%乙醇浸渍法获得。幼虫在五个浓度(0.6%、0.8%、1.0%、1.2%和1.5%)下进行测试,观察时间为3、6、12和24小时。数据通过Kruskal–Wallis检验、Mann–Whitney事后检验和Probit分析进行分析,以确定LC50、LC90、LT50和LT90。姜黄根提取物的制备在帕朗卡拉大学医学院生物医学实验室I进行,而幼虫杀灭测试则在南加里曼丹省坦布布县公共卫生实验室中心进行,时间为2025年7月至10月。结果:幼虫死亡率随着浓度的增加和暴露时间的延长而增加。Kruskal–Wallis检验显示不同浓度之间存在显著差异(p < 0.05)。LC50为0.614%,LC90为1.459%,而LT50为5.613小时,LT90为15.102小时。活性代谢产物被认为对幼虫死亡率的增加有所贡献。结论:姜黄根提取物对白纹伊蚊三龄幼虫表现出有效的幼虫杀灭活性,其效果随着提取物浓度和暴露时间的增加而增强。这些发现为姜黄根作为环保型植物源幼虫杀灭剂的潜在应用提供了科学依据,并有助于开发可持续的登革热控制替代策略。

news.content: Skip to main content Help Log in ReliefWeb Search Content Search What are you looking for? Search|t Updates Countries Disasters Organizations Topics Jobs Training Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA World + 8 more Epidemic and emerging disease alerts in the Pacific as of 10 November 2026 Format Map Source SPC Posted 10 Nov 2026 Originally published 10 Nov 2026 Attachments Download Map (PDF | 546.03 KB) Highlights/updates since the last map was sent on PacNet on 03 November 2026: Dengue • Marshall Islands: The 18th Outbreak Situation Report covering 15 August to 02 November 2026, records 171 positive cases (confirmed and probable) among 582 specimens tested: Majuro 128 and Ebeye 43, against 127 and 40 in the 17th Outbreak Situation report covering 15 August to 29 October 2026. There have been 15 hospitalisations and no deaths since the beginning of the outbreak, and no patient is currently admitted. Attack rates are 5.5 per 1,000 population in Majuro and 4.4 per 1,000 in Ebeye, while positivity rates are 28% and 36%, respectively. Cases are still being reported at a low, steady rate. Only DENV-1 has been identified. The red alert for dengue (DENV-1) remains in effect. – Source: Republic of the Marshall Islands Ministry of Health and Human Services, 17th and 18th Outbreak Situation Reports on dengue fever in Majuro and Ebeye shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 07 November 2026. • Samoa: Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report Issue No. 80, covering EpiWeek 43 (19 to 25 October 2026), reports 30 new cases, down 43% on the previous week, with two laboratory-confirmed cases, the first since EpiWeek 40, two new admissions and no death. Since 1st January 2025, there has been 20,510 clinically diagnosed cases, 5,549 laboratory-confirmed cases and nine dengue-related deaths that have been recorded. DENV-1 accounts for 52% and DENV-2 for 48% of serotyped cases, and children under 15 years for 73% of cases. The blue alert for dengue (DENV-1 & DENV-2) remains in effect. – Source: Ministry of Health Samoa, Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report Issue No. 80 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 04 November 2026. Measles • Papua New Guinea: The National Department of Health weekly bulletin for EpiWeek 44 (26 October to 1st November 2026) reports 11 acute fever and rash cases nationally, down from 31 in EpiWeek 43 (revised from 26). Year to date, 464 cases have been reported and 406 samples tested, with 19 IgM-positive measles results. After Expert Review Group review, two measles cases (New Ireland 1, Western Highlands 1) and two rubella cases are confirmed in 2026. The last IgM-positive measles onset was on 15 September 2026 and the last rubella onset on 29 September 2026. The measles-rubella vaccination campaign targets all children under seven in districts with a detected case. The red alert for measles is changed to a blue alert for Papua New Guinea. – Source: Papua New Guinea National Department of Health, Public Health Events Weekly Bulletin shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 08 November 2026. Respiratory diseases • French Polynesia: In EpiWeek 44 (26 October to 1st November 2026), French Polynesia remained in an influenza epidemic phase, with 94 laboratory-confirmed cases, mainly influenza A and predominantly subtype H1N1. A total of 32 hospitalisations and three deaths are reported. Viral circulation is currently detected in Tahiti, Raiatea, the Marquesas and the Tuamotu. Since the start of the epidemic phase, the health surveillance office no longer processes nasopharyngeal samples taken for PCR detection of respiratory pathogens for surveillance purposes. The red alert for influenza A remains in effect for French Polynesia. – Source: Agence de régulation de l'action sanitaire et sociale (ARASS), Bulletin de Surveillance Sanitaire de Polynésie française n°39 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 10 November 2026. • Vanuatu: On 03 November 2026, the Ministry of Health reported that an influenza A outbreak has been officially declared on Tanna Island, Tafea Province, following increased influenza-like illness activity and laboratory-confirmed influenza A cases. A total of 163 influenza-like illness cases were reported on Tanna. From EpiWeek 39 to 43, clinically diagnosed influenza cases fluctuated but increased overall, exceeding the alert threshold in EpiWeeks 40, 41 and 43. Of 28 samples tested, 11 were positive for influenza A. Two severe cases were reported, with no hospital admission so far. A provincial health emergency operations centre is coordinating the response. In Shefa Province, the Shefa Community Health Service has issued a health alert stating that influenza remains present on Efate Island and calling for the protection of vulnerable people: children, pregnant women, the elderly, people with disabilities and people with non-communicable diseases. The red alert for influenza A remains in effect for Vanuatu. – Sources: Vanuatu Ministry of Health, official statement on Facebook and Shefa Community Health Service, Shefa Health Alert on Facebook accessed on 10 November 2026. • Wallis and Futuna: On 06 November 2026, the Agence de Santé de Wallis et Futuna declared an influenza epidemic. To avoid overloading the emergency department, opening hours of the Hahake dispensary only are extended from 07 to 11 November 2026 inclusive. The Agency case definition for influenza includes sudden onset of fever of 38°C or above, chills, fatigue, cough or sore throat. No case count or influenza type has been reported. A grey alert for influenza-like illness is issued for Wallis and Futuna. – Source: Agence de Santé de Wallis et Futuna, press release of 06 November 2026 on Facebook accessed on 10 November 2026. Other Information: Dengue • Hawai’i: On 04 November 2026, the Hawaiʻi State Department of Health reported a new travel-related dengue case on Oʻahu, in a person exposed while travelling in a region where dengue is common, bringing to 11 the dengue cases recorded in Hawaiʻi in 2026. Ten of the 11 cases involved travel to Pacific Island countries and territories and one to another dengue-endemic area outside the Pacific. The Department is carrying out inspections and mosquito control, and the risk of local transmission is expected to be low. – Source: Hawaiʻi Department of Health, DOH reports 11th travel-related dengue virus case of 2026, accessed on 10 November 2026. Leptospirosis • Australia: On 05 November 2026, the Northern Territory Centre for Disease Control issued a health alert reporting 11 leptospirosis cases in the Northern Territory in 2026, against an average of 10 a year. Four cases have required intensive care, and one death has been reported. Areas associated with cases include Fogg Dam and Harrison Dam, Oenpelli, the Arnhem Land wetlands, Finniss River and Tipperary Station, as well as rural Darwin and the Katherine district around water and flooding events. – Sources: Northern Territory Centre for Disease Control, health alert on leptospirosis and BEACON, Fatal case of leptospirosis after hunting near a billabong in Northern Territory, Australia, amid rising 2026 caseload accessed on 10 November 2026. Pertussis/Whooping cough • New Zealand: Twenty-one Auckland schools and early childhood centres reported pertussis cases in the past month, up from four such settings in September, with 37 cases in Auckland over the past three weeks. Health New Zealand states that the situation is not at epidemic or outbreak level and that public health teams are monitoring it closely. Case numbers are very low elsewhere in New Zealand. Nationally, 1,537 cases have been notified in 2026 as of 30 October 2026. – Sources: Pertussis dashboard and BEACON, Twenty-one schools and childcare centers in Auckland, New Zealand report pertussis cases within weeks of school holidays ending accessed on 10 November 2026. news.content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home Culture – Society Y tế Dengue fever cases are on the rise; be vigilant for the risk of serious complications. In the first 10 months of 2026, the whole country recorded more than 170,000 cases of dengue fever, a 26% increase compared to the same period last year. Notably, all four types of dengue virus are circulating in many localities. Experts advise people not to be complacent about the initial signs and to proactively prevent the disease to reduce the risk of complications and death. Báo Phú Thọ•11/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 The number of cases is increasing, and the course of the epidemic is unpredictable. According to the Ministry of Health , in the first 10 months of 2026, the whole country recorded 170,684 cases of dengue fever and 21 deaths, an increase of 26% compared to the same period in 2025. The South accounted for 66.8% of the total cases, followed by the Central Highlands at 17.5%, the Central region at 9.8%, and the North at 5.9%. In Ho Chi Minh City, by the end of week 43, the city had recorded over 42,500 cases of dengue fever, including 11 deaths. Di An ward alone accounted for 861 cases and one child death. Khám phá thêm Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch Khám phá ĐNA Đọc Tin Tức Notably, the epidemiological characteristics of dengue fever are changing. While previously the disease typically increased sharply during the rainy season, mainly concentrated in the South and Central regions, dengue fever can now occur year-round in many localities, including some mountainous provinces in the North such as Tuyen Quang and Son La . Along with the expansion of its distribution area, all four dengue virus types, DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4, have been recorded in Vietnam. Of these, DENV-3 reappeared from the end of 2024 after many years of infrequent recording. Surveillance results in the southern region in September 2026 showed that DENV-2 accounted for 69% and DENV-1 accounted for 27.5% of the samples with identified virus types. According to experts, people who have previously had dengue fever can still be reinfected because the immunity acquired after the illness does not provide adequate protection against other types of the virus. In some cases, reinfection can even lead to severe illness. Dr. Hoang Minh Duc, Director of the Department of Disease Prevention (Ministry of Health), stated that despite Vietnam's implementation of numerous prevention and control measures, dengue fever remains an endemic disease with a high incidence rate. This reality necessitates continued evaluation of the effectiveness of existing solutions, updating scientific advancements, and selecting disease prevention methods appropriate to practical conditions. Tìm hiểu lịch sử You may also like Not only is dengue fever increasing in number, but it is also concerning because of its potential for severe complications and damage to multiple organs. The disease often begins with symptoms such as high fever, headache, eye pain, muscle and joint pain, or nausea, which can easily be mistaken for common viral infections. According to Professor Nguyen Van Kinh, former Director of the Central Hospital for Tropical Diseases, the period from the third to the seventh day of the illness requires special monitoring. When the patient's fever begins to subside, the risk of plasma leakage, shock, and serious complications can still occur. Young children, the elderly, and individuals with underlying conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, or obesity require close monitoring due to their higher risk of complications. Take proactive measures to prevent disease, don't wait for an outbreak to occur. Given the unpredictable nature of dengue fever, experts emphasize the need to shift from responding to outbreaks when they occur to proactive, ongoing prevention efforts within the community. Dengue fever is primarily transmitted through the Aedes aegypti mosquito. The mosquito bites an infected person and can then transmit the disease to a healthy person through subsequent bites. Notably, Aedes mosquitoes can breed even in small water containers around the house. Therefore, simply spraying insecticides when an outbreak occurs is not enough to control the risk of transmission. Families should regularly clean and cover water containers, remove items that can collect water, collect waste, and dispose of breeding grounds. At the same time, they should proactively prevent mosquito bites using appropriate measures such as using mosquito nets, wearing long-sleeved clothing, or using mosquito repellent products as directed, even during the day. You may also like Along with controlling disease-carrying mosquitoes, early detection and proper monitoring of the disease's progression are crucial in limiting complications. Individuals suspected of having dengue fever should be examined, have their risk assessed, and follow the instructions of healthcare professionals, especially during the stage when the disease may become severe. Symptoms such as severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, unusual bleeding, lethargy, extreme fatigue, or cold hands and feet require urgent medical evaluation. Patients should not rely solely on the reduction of fever to conclude that their condition is improving, and should avoid self-medicating with inappropriate drugs. With all four types of Dengue virus circulating, the risk of reinfection remains. Vaccination is a preventive measure that should be advised based on age, health status, and professional guidance, and must be combined with measures to prevent mosquito bites. https://daidoanket.vn/chuyen-muc/suc-khoe.html According to daidoanket.vn Source: Báo Phú Thọ Original articleCopy https://baophutho.vn/sot-xuat-huyet-gia-tang-canh-giac-nguy-co-bien-chung-nang-264205.htm Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Tag: Riskdeathrecorded#Contracted dengue fevervirusdisease preventionCentral Hospital for Tropical DiseasescomplicationscirculateChuyên gia Comment (0) Top Interests Newest Please leave a comment to share your feelings! analysis.brief_en: Dengue fever is on the rise in Vietnam, with over 170,684 cases reported in the first 10 months of 2026, a 26% increase compared to the same period in 2025. The South region accounted for 66.8% of these cases, followed by the Central Highlands, Central region, and North. In Ho Chi Minh City, more than 42,500 cases and 11 deaths were recorded by the end of week 43, while Di An ward alone reported 861 cases and one child death. All four dengue virus types—DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4—are circulating, with DENV-3 reappearing after years of infrequent recording. The disease is now occurring year-round, not just during the rainy season, and experts warn that reinfection can lead to severe illness. The Ministry of Health highlights the need for continued evaluation of prevention strategies and emphasizes proactive community efforts to reduce the risk of complications and deaths. Individuals should monitor symptoms closely, especially during the third to seventh day of illness, and avoid self-medication. Families are advised to clean water containers and take measures to prevent mosquito bites, as these are the primary transmission routes.

news.title_zh: 登革热案件呈上升趋势;警惕严重并发症的风险。- 越南.vn
news.source_body_en: Dengue fever is on the rise in Vietnam, with over 170,684 cases reported in the first 10 months of 2026, a 26% increase compared to the same period in 2025. The South region accounted for 66.8% of these cases, followed by the Central Highlands, Central region, and North. In Ho Chi Minh City, more than 42,500 cases and 11 deaths were recorded by the end of week 43, while Di An ward alone reported 861 cases and one child death. All four dengue virus types—DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4—are circulating, with DENV-3 reappearing after years of infrequent recording. The disease is now occurring year-round, not just during the rainy season, and experts warn that reinfection can lead to severe illness. The Ministry of Health highlights the need for continued evaluation of prevention strategies and emphasizes proactive community efforts to reduce the risk of complications and deaths. Individuals should monitor symptoms closely, especially during the third to seventh day of illness, and avoid self-medication. Families are advised to clean water containers and take measures to prevent mosquito bites, as these are the primary transmission routes.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 12, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Dengue Virus Evades Innate Antiviral Defenses as Dysregulated Death Pathways Drive Severe Pathology by November 11, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Dengue Virus Evades Innate Antiviral Defenses as Dysregulated Death Pathways Drive Severe Pathology Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A narrative review examining dengue virus literature published between 2000 and 2026 establishes that disease severity is driven primarily by host immune reactions rather than viral replication alone. Dengue virus, an RNA pathogen belonging to the genus Flavivirus within the family Flaviviridae, comprises four antigenically distinct serotypes, DENV-1 through DENV-4, differing by twenty-five to thirty percent at the amino acid level. Primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes across tropical and subtropical regions, the virus infects an estimated 3.6 billion people in over one hundred countries, causing hundreds of millions of annual infections. Inoculation into host skin initiates infection before the virus disseminates through the lymphatic system and bloodstream to infect the spleen and liver. While clinical manifestations range from asymptomatic infection and classic dengue fever to severe hemorrhagic fever and shock syndrome, review findings demonstrate that life-threatening plasma leakage and hemorrhage stem from critically dysregulated innate immune pathways and uncontrolled inflammatory responses. Innate immune defense begins with pattern-recognition receptors detecting conserved pathogen-associated molecular patterns to trigger type I interferons and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Endosomal Toll-like receptors execute essential nucleic acid surveillance: Toll-like receptor 3 recognizes viral double-stranded RNA replication intermediates, whereas Toll-like receptor 7 detects single-stranded RNA rich in guanosine and uridine. Predominantly expressed in dendritic cells, monocytes, and macrophages, these receptors engage specialized intracellular adapters upon ligand binding. Toll-like receptor 3 signals through TIR-domain-containing adapter inducing interferon-β, while Toll-like receptor 7 relies on myeloid differentiation primary response 88. These adapters recruit tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factors, activating TANK-binding kinase 1 and IκB kinase complexes. Phosphorylation of interferon regulatory factors 3 and 7 alongside nuclear factor-κB induces type I interferons and cytokines such as interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α. Subsequent interferon binding to cell-surface receptors stimulates JAK-STAT signaling, phosphorylating STAT1 and STAT2 to induce interferon-stimulated genes, although excessive pathway activation fosters severe immunopathology. Within the cytosolic compartment, the RIG-I-like receptor family serves as a frontline surveillance network for sensing dengue viral RNA. This pathway utilizes two key sensors: retinoic acid-inducible gene I, which detects short double-stranded or single-stranded viral RNA bearing 5′-triphosphate or 5′-diphosphate groups, and melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5, which recognizes long double-stranded RNA. Ligand binding prompts conformational shifts exposing caspase activation and recruitment domains, which bind mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein on the outer mitochondrial membrane. Mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein subsequently functions as an organizing platform to recruit tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factors, TANK-binding kinase 1, and IκB kinase-ε. These kinases phosphorylate interferon regulatory factors 3 and 7, prompting dimerization and nuclear translocation, while concurrently stimulating nuclear factor-κB. This concerted transcription produces type I interferons that act in autocrine and paracrine loops through interferon receptors, driving JAK-STAT signaling and interferon-stimulated gene synthesis to establish an antiviral cellular state. Discover more Engineering job board Research publication platform Scientific instrument sales Laboratory equipment supplier Biotech startup funding Although dengue virus possesses an RNA genome that does not directly bind cytosolic DNA sensors, the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase and stimulator of interferon genes pathway contributes indirectly to antiviral defense. Cellular stress and mitochondrial damage induced by infection trigger the release of host mitochondrial DNA into the cytosol. Cytosolic DNA activates cyclic GMP-AMP synthase to generate the second messenger 2′3′-cyclic GMP-AMP, which binds stimulator of interferon genes localized in the endoplasmic reticulum. Once activated, stimulator of interferon genes recruits TANK-binding kinase 1 to phosphorylate interferon regulatory factor 3, stimulating type I interferon expression alongside nuclear factor-κB-dependent pro-inflammatory cytokines. However, the review emphasizes that this indirect DNA-sensing response varies considerably across experimental cell types and infection conditions. Consequently, evidence derived from laboratory models regarding the protective magnitude of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase axis must be interpreted cautiously before extrapolating findings directly to human dengue pathogenesis. Dengue virus deploys nonstructural proteins to systematically counter host innate signaling at multiple biochemical steps. Nonstructural protein NS3 binds the chaperone 14-3-3ε to block retinoic acid-inducible gene I translocation, while NS4A disrupts its association with mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein, particularly in serotype 1. Furthermore, nonstructural proteins NS2A and NS4B inhibit TANK-binding kinase 1 activation and interferon regulatory factor 3 phosphorylation across serotypes 1, 2, and 4. The pathogen also targets cytosolic DNA sensing: NS2B promotes cyclic GMP-AMP synthase degradation via an autophagy-lysosomal pathway, and the NS2B/3 protease cleaves human stimulator of interferon genes to disrupt downstream antiviral transcription. Downstream of interferon reception, nonstructural proteins NS2A, NS4A, and NS4B inhibit STAT1 phosphorylation, while NS5 binds STAT2 to trigger its proteasomal degradation. By dismantling the STAT1-STAT2-IRF9 complex, the virus suppresses interferon-stimulated gene transcription, enabling viral persistence and promoting disease progression. Cell death receptor signaling provides a delicate equilibrium between eliminating infected cells and causing host tissue damage. Ligation of surface death receptors, including Fas, tumor necrosis factor receptor 1, and TRAIL receptors, initiates extrinsic apoptosis through the death-inducing signaling complex containing Fas-associated death domain protein and procaspase-8. Cleaved caspase-8 activates executioner caspases 3 and 7 to execute cellular death. In early infection, apoptosis restricts viral amplification by destroying infected host cells; however, excessive receptor activation precipitates severe complications. Clinical data link increased disease severity to elevated circulating levels of tumor necrosis factor-α, Fas ligand, and TRAIL. Unrestrained apoptosis of vascular endothelial cells disrupts barrier integrity, causing plasma leakage and vascular shock. Similarly, widespread lymphocyte apoptosis impairs adaptive immunity. Meanwhile, nuclear factor-κB signaling can counteract apoptosis by transcribing antiapoptotic genes, including BCL-2, BCL-XL, and XIAP, generating a fragile balance between cell survival and inflammatory tissue destruction. Accurate pathology assessment requires distinguishing apoptosis from alternative regulated cell death modes, specifically necroptosis and pyroptosis. Apoptosis depends on caspases and maintains plasma membrane integrity early, restricting intracellular content release. In contrast, necroptosis is a lytic, pro-inflammatory process driven by receptor-interacting protein kinase 1, receptor-interacting protein kinase 3, and mixed-lineage kinase domain-like protein. Under normal conditions, caspase-8 prevents necroptosis by cleaving receptor-interacting protein kinases 1 and 3; when caspase-8 is suppressed, necroptosis ensues. Pyroptosis represents another distinct inflammatory death mechanism, mediated by inflammatory caspases and gasdermin proteins that form plasma membrane pores to release inflammatory mediators. The review emphasizes that although these cell death pathways intersect, they are mechanistically separate. Assertions that necroptosis or pyroptosis drive dengue pathology require explicit biochemical confirmation, such as mixed-lineage kinase domain-like protein activation or gasdermin cleavage, rather than theoretical assumptions drawn from unrelated viral infections. Translating innate immune concepts into dengue vaccines highlights major challenges regarding safety and serotype-specific protection, as demonstrated by licensed vaccines CYD-TDV and TAK-003. CYD-TDV, a live-attenuated chimeric vaccine on a yellow fever 17D backbone given in three doses over twelve months, increased the risk of severe disease in seronegative recipients, requiring pre-vaccination screening before its manufacturer discontinued production due to low demand. Conversely, TAK-003 is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine with a DENV-2 backbone given in two doses three months apart, recommended by the World Health Organization for children aged six to sixteen in high-transmission areas. However, protection varies by serotype and baseline serostatus. Developing future vaccines requires balanced, durable tetravalent protection without provoking antibody-dependent enhancement. Adjuvants targeting innate pathways, including Toll-like receptor agonists, are under evaluation to enhance antigen presentation, though candidate formulations require rigorous safety testing to prevent excessive inflammation. Therapeutic strategies under investigation target both viral enzymatic machinery and host immune pathways to curb viral replication and inflammation. The viral NS2B/3 protease represents a prominent target because selective inhibitors could simultaneously block viral polyprotein processing and protect human stimulator of interferon genes from cleavage. Nevertheless, NS2B/3 inhibitors remain experimental, requiring improvements in selectivity, intracellular potency, and post-symptomatic efficacy. Host-directed interventions targeting innate pathways, including STING agonists such as cAIMP and diABZI or investigational Toll-like receptor agonists, stimulate protective type I interferons but pose risks of severe cytokine release and tissue toxicity. Similarly, exogenous interferon therapy faces administration timing constraints. Interventions modulating cell death, such as pan-caspase inhibitor z-VAD-FMK, BCL-2 inhibitor venetoclax, inhibitor of apoptosis protein antagonist xevinapant, and TRAIL receptor agonists, remain in preclinical stages. Because untargeted apoptotic modulation could destroy healthy tissue or hinder viral clearance, none has demonstrated clinical efficacy in dengue. Critical research gaps continue to hinder the translation of innate immune and apoptotic pathway modulators into approved clinical therapies for dengue. Detailed mechanisms explaining how viral nonstructural proteins differentially affect pattern-recognition signaling across immune and vascular endothelial cells remain incompletely defined. Additionally, the precise biochemical threshold separating protective antiviral defense from destructive immunopathology remains unresolved, as does the role of cell death in promoting vascular leakage. Existing research relies heavily on in vitro and animal models that fail to capture human disease dynamics, underscoring the need for organoid platforms and multi-omics profiling to identify reliable severity biomarkers. Because no targeted therapeutic has proven effective enough to replace supportive fluid therapy, future clinical success will depend on identifying suitable therapeutic windows and developing combination regimens that couple direct-acting antivirals with host-directed modulators to control viral replication without triggering tissue damage. Dengue virus, an RNA pathogen belonging to the genus Flavivirus within the family Flaviviridae, comprises four antigenically distinct serotypes, DENV-1 through DENV-4, differing by twenty-five to thirty percent at the amino acid level. Primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes across tropical and subtropical regions, the virus infects an estimated 3.6 billion people in over one hundred countries, causing hundreds of millions of annual infections. Inoculation into host skin initiates infection before the virus disseminates through the lymphatic system and bloodstream to infect the spleen and liver. While clinical manifestations range from asymptomatic infection and classic dengue fever to severe hemorrhagic fever and shock syndrome, review findings demonstrate that life-threatening plasma leakage and hemorrhage stem from critically dysregulated innate immune pathways and uncontrolled inflammatory responses. Innate immune defense begins with pattern-recognition receptors detecting conserved pathogen-associated molecular patterns to trigger type I interferons and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Endosomal Toll-like receptors execute essential nucleic acid surveillance: Toll-like receptor 3 recognizes viral double-stranded RNA replication intermediates, whereas Toll-like receptor 7 detects single-stranded RNA rich in guanosine and uridine. Predominantly expressed in dendritic cells, monocytes, and macrophages, these receptors engage specialized intracellular adapters upon ligand binding. Toll-like receptor 3 signals through TIR-domain-containing adapter inducing interferon-β, while Toll-like receptor 7 relies on myeloid differentiation primary response 88. These adapters recruit tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factors, activating TANK-binding kinase 1 and IκB kinase complexes. Phosphorylation of interferon regulatory factors 3 and 7 alongside nuclear factor-κB induces type I interferons and cytokines such as interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α. Subsequent interferon binding to cell-surface receptors stimulates JAK-STAT signaling, phosphorylating STAT1 and STAT2 to induce interferon-stimulated genes, although excessive pathway activation fosters severe immunopathology. Within the cytosolic compartment, the RIG-I-like receptor family serves as a frontline surveillance network for sensing dengue viral RNA. This pathway utilizes two key sensors: retinoic acid-inducible gene I, which detects short double-stranded or single-stranded viral RNA bearing 5′-triphosphate or 5′-diphosphate groups, and melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5, which recognizes long double-stranded RNA. Ligand binding prompts conformational shifts exposing caspase activation and recruitment domains, which bind mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein on the outer mitochondrial membrane. Mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein subsequently functions as an organizing platform to recruit tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factors, TANK-binding kinase 1, and IκB kinase-ε. These kinases phosphorylate interferon regulatory factors 3 and 7, prompting dimerization and nuclear translocation, while concurrently stimulating nuclear factor-κB. This concerted transcription produces type I interferons that act in autocrine and paracrine loops through interferon receptors, driving JAK-STAT signaling and interferon-stimulated gene synthesis to establish an antiviral cellular state. Discover more Engineering job board Research publication platform Scientific instrument sales Laboratory equipment supplier Biotech startup funding Although dengue virus possesses an RNA genome that does not directly bind cytosolic DNA sensors, the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase and stimulator of interferon genes pathway contributes indirectly to antiviral defense. Cellular stress and mitochondrial damage induced by infection trigger the release of host mitochondrial DNA into the cytosol. Cytosolic DNA activates cyclic GMP-AMP synthase to generate the second messenger 2′3′-cyclic GMP-AMP, which binds stimulator of interferon genes localized in the endoplasmic reticulum. Once activated, stimulator of interferon genes recruits TANK-binding kinase 1 to phosphorylate interferon regulatory factor 3, stimulating type I interferon expression alongside nuclear factor-κB-dependent pro-inflammatory cytokines. However, the review emphasizes that this indirect DNA-sensing response varies considerably across experimental cell types and infection conditions. Consequently, evidence derived from laboratory models regarding the protective magnitude of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase axis must be interpreted cautiously before extrapolating findings directly to human dengue pathogenesis. Dengue virus deploys nonstructural proteins to systematically counter host innate signaling at multiple biochemical steps. Nonstructural protein NS3 binds the chaperone 14-3-3ε to block retinoic acid-inducible gene I translocation, while NS4A disrupts its association with mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein, particularly in serotype 1. Furthermore, nonstructural proteins NS2A and NS4B inhibit TANK-binding kinase 1 activation and interferon regulatory factor 3 phosphorylation across serotypes 1, 2, and 4. The pathogen also targets cytosolic DNA sensing: NS2B promotes cyclic GMP-AMP synthase degradation via an autophagy-lysosomal pathway, and the NS2B/3 protease cleaves human stimulator of interferon genes to disrupt downstream antiviral transcription. Downstream of interferon reception, nonstructural proteins NS2A, NS4A, and NS4B inhibit STAT1 phosphorylation, while NS5 binds STAT2 to trigger its proteasomal degradation. By dismantling the STAT1-STAT2-IRF9 complex, the virus suppresses interferon-stimulated gene transcription, enabling viral persistence and promoting disease progression. Cell death receptor signaling provides a delicate equilibrium between eliminating infected cells and causing host tissue damage. Ligation of surface death receptors, including Fas, tumor necrosis factor receptor 1, and TRAIL receptors, initiates extrinsic apoptosis through the death-inducing signaling complex containing Fas-associated death domain protein and procaspase-8. Cleaved caspase-8 activates executioner caspases 3 and 7 to execute cellular death. In early infection, apoptosis restricts viral amplification by destroying infected host cells; however, excessive receptor activation precipitates severe complications. Clinical data link increased disease severity to elevated circulating levels of tumor necrosis factor-α, Fas ligand, and TRAIL. Unrestrained apoptosis of vascular endothelial cells disrupts barrier integrity, causing plasma leakage and vascular shock. Similarly, widespread lymphocyte apoptosis impairs adaptive immunity. Meanwhile, nuclear factor-κB signaling can counteract apoptosis by transcribing antiapoptotic genes, including BCL-2, BCL-XL, and XIAP, generating a fragile balance between cell survival and inflammatory tissue destruction. Accurate pathology assessment requires distinguishing apoptosis from alternative regulated cell death modes, specifically necroptosis and pyroptosis. Apoptosis depends on caspases and maintains plasma membrane integrity early, restricting intracellular content release. In contrast, necroptosis is a lytic, pro-inflammatory process driven by receptor-interacting protein kinase 1, receptor-interacting protein kinase 3, and mixed-lineage kinase domain-like protein. Under normal conditions, caspase-8 prevents necroptosis by cleaving receptor-interacting protein kinases 1 and 3; when caspase-8 is suppressed, necroptosis ensues. Pyroptosis represents another distinct inflammatory death mechanism, mediated by inflammatory caspases and gasdermin proteins that form plasma membrane pores to release inflammatory mediators. The review emphasizes that although these cell death pathways intersect, they are mechanistically separate. Assertions that necroptosis or pyroptosis drive dengue pathology require explicit biochemical confirmation, such as mixed-lineage kinase domain-like protein activation or gasdermin cleavage, rather than theoretical assumptions drawn from unrelated viral infections. Translating innate immune concepts into dengue vaccines highlights major challenges regarding safety and serotype-specific protection, as demonstrated by licensed vaccines CYD-TDV and TAK-003. CYD-TDV, a live-attenuated chimeric vaccine on a yellow fever 17D backbone given in three doses over twelve months, increased the risk of severe disease in seronegative recipients, requiring pre-vaccination screening before its manufacturer discontinued production due to low demand. Conversely, TAK-003 is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine with a DENV-2 backbone given in two doses three months apart, recommended by the World Health Organization for children aged six to sixteen in high-transmission areas. However, protection varies by serotype and baseline serostatus. Developing future vaccines requires balanced, durable tetravalent protection without provoking antibody-dependent enhancement. Adjuvants targeting innate pathways, including Toll-like receptor agonists, are under evaluation to enhance antigen presentation, though candidate formulations require rigorous safety testing to prevent excessive inflammation. Therapeutic strategies under investigation target both viral enzymatic machinery and host immune pathways to curb viral replication and inflammation. The viral NS2B/3 protease represents a prominent target because selective inhibitors could simultaneously block viral polyprotein processing and protect human stimulator of interferon genes from cleavage. Nevertheless, NS2B/3 inhibitors remain experimental, requiring improvements in selectivity, intracellular potency, and post-symptomatic efficacy. Host-directed interventions targeting innate pathways, including STING agonists such as cAIMP and diABZI or investigational Toll-like receptor agonists, stimulate protective type I interferons but pose risks of severe cytokine release and tissue toxicity. Similarly, exogenous interferon therapy faces administration timing constraints. Interventions modulating cell death, such as pan-caspase inhibitor z-VAD-FMK, BCL-2 inhibitor venetoclax, inhibitor of apoptosis protein antagonist xevinapant, and TRAIL receptor agonists, remain in preclinical stages. Because untargeted apoptotic modulation could destroy healthy tissue or hinder viral clearance, none has demonstrated clinical efficacy in dengue. Critical research gaps continue to hinder the translation of innate immune and apoptotic pathway modulators into approved clinical therapies for dengue. Detailed mechanisms explaining how viral nonstructural proteins differentially affect pattern-recognition signaling across immune and vascular endothelial cells remain incompletely defined. Additionally, the precise biochemical threshold separating protective antiviral defense from destructive immunopathology remains unresolved, as does the role of cell death in promoting vascular leakage. Existing research relies heavily on in vitro and animal models that fail to capture human disease dynamics, underscoring the need for organoid platforms and multi-omics profiling to identify reliable severity biomarkers. Because no targeted therapeutic has proven effective enough to replace supportive fluid therapy, future clinical success will depend on identifying suitable therapeutic windows and developing combination regimens that couple direct-acting antivirals with host-directed modulators to control viral replication without triggering tissue damage. news.content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home Culture – Society Y tế With dengue fever cases exceeding 170,000, we cannot rely solely on mosquito control. Dengue fever is becoming increasingly complex, with over 170,000 cases and 21 deaths in the first 10 months of 2026. Worryingly, the disease no longer follows a clear seasonal pattern, and its distribution areas are expanding. This reality demands a new approach and a strengthening of proactive prevention measures. Check Symptoms Hà Nội Mới•06/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Hanoi is disseminating information on dengue fever prevention and control measures to households. Photo: Hanoi Department of Health . 21 deaths in 10 months At the Dengue Fever Conference 2026, held on November 6-11 and chaired by the Department of Disease Prevention ( Ministry of Health ) in collaboration with many other units, experts warned that dengue fever continues to be a worrying health burden in Vietnam. Check Symptoms Discover more Check Symptoms Find Treatments Buy Bug Kits According to information released at the conference, in the first 10 months of 2026, the whole country recorded 170,684 cases of dengue fever (a 1.3-fold increase compared to the same period in 2025), including 21 deaths. Notably, the disease is endemic year-round in all provinces and cities and is spreading to even mountainous areas in the North such as Tuyen Quang and Son La - areas that previously recorded few cases. Dr. Hoang Minh Duc, Director of the Department of Disease Prevention (Ministry of Health), speaks at the conference. Photo: Organizing Committee. The expansion of dengue fever's prevalence and the increasing number of cases indicate that dengue prevention and control efforts are facing numerous challenges. Speaking at the conference, Dr. Hoang Minh Duc, Director of the Department of Disease Prevention (Ministry of Health), stated that despite the health sector implementing many measures, mobilizing resources from the central to local levels, and coordinating with domestic and international experts, disease control has not yet achieved sustainable effectiveness. Check Symptoms One factor complicating the dengue fever situation is the circulation of all four dengue virus serotypes: DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4 in Vietnam. The prevalence of these serotypes varies over time and across regions. The movement of serotypes, combined with climate change, rapid urbanization, and mosquito resistance to insecticides, makes predicting and controlling outbreaks increasingly difficult. You may also like People's Physician - Professor Dr. Nguyen Van Kinh, former Director of the Central Hospital for Tropical Diseases , believes that the increasing trend in dengue fever cases, which no longer follows a clear seasonal or cyclical pattern as before, is partly due to climate change and increased rainfall, creating favorable conditions for disease-transmitting mosquitoes to breed and develop. Find Treatments According to Professor Nguyen Van Kinh, although the mortality rate recorded in Vietnam is currently low (about 0.01%), dengue fever remains a disease with complex and unpredictable clinical course. The severity varies from person to person, depending on immune response, age, immune status, and underlying medical conditions. In particular, more than 90% of people infected with the Dengue virus are asymptomatic but can still participate in the disease transmission cycle through mosquitoes carrying the virus. Regarding treatment, Professor Nguyen Van Kinh stated that there is currently no specific drug for dengue fever, and treatment mainly focuses on managing symptoms, controlling shock, and preventing severe complications. During outbreaks, the overcrowding in hospitals continues to put significant pressure on the medical staff. Expanding proactive disease prevention strategies. Given the increasingly unpredictable nature of dengue fever, focusing solely on controlling outbreaks or eradicating mosquitoes when cases increase is insufficient. Experts believe that a strong shift towards proactive prevention is needed, combining multiple solutions to reduce the risk of infection within the community. Vaccination is considered an additional preventive tool alongside measures to control disease-carrying mosquitoes. Check Symptoms Conference scene. Photo: Organizing Committee At the conference, experiences in implementing vaccination programs in several countries provided further practical evidence of the role of vaccines in disease prevention and control. Dr. Rosana Richtmann, Director of the Infection Control Committee (ICC) at Santa Joana Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital and former President of the Infectious Diseases Society of São Paulo State ( Brazil ), stated that Brazil has included the dengue fever vaccine in its public immunization program since 2024. The program was initially implemented in 521 localities, then expanded to 2,752 localities, with a total of 24 million doses of vaccine distributed. Notably, actual data from São Paulo state in 2024-2025 showed that receiving two doses reduced the risk of symptomatic dengue fever by 73.1% and the risk of hospitalization by 87.9%. The protective effect is maintained even if the DENV-3 virus type reappears. You may also like Not only in Brazil, but also in Indonesia , vaccines are being deployed in combination with medical technology applications to enhance proactive prevention in high-risk areas. In Vietnam, the dengue fever vaccine currently in circulation is the first and only one approved by the Ministry of Health. The vaccine has achieved pre-qualification by the World Health Organization (WHO) for quality, safety, and efficacy, and is recommended by the WHO for use in countries with a high burden of dengue fever. To date, the vaccine has been approved in 43 countries, with over 32 million doses distributed globally; it has also been implemented in public immunization programs in Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Indonesia, Honduras, Paraguay, Peru, and Thailand. To ensure the effectiveness of dengue prevention and control strategies, experts once again emphasized the need for the simultaneous implementation of three groups of solutions: vaccination to prevent the disease; mosquito eradication and elimination of larvae to reduce the risk of transmission; and early detection and timely treatment to limit complications and mortality. Each solution plays a distinct role but is closely related and complements the others. Combining these measures regularly and continuously will contribute to controlling the epidemic and reducing the burden of dengue fever in the community.
