supplementary_news.content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home Culture – Society Y tế Dengue fever is on the rise, and doctors warn of the most critical period. Nationwide, more than 170,000 cases of dengue fever have been recorded, with 21 deaths. Doctors warn of the dangerous phase when the fever begins to subside. Check Symptoms Báo Gia đình và Xã hội•07/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 According to statistics from the Ministry of Health , in the first 10 months of 2026, the whole country recorded more than 170,000 cases of dengue fever and 21 deaths. Meanwhile, the same period in 2025 recorded approximately 106,000 cases. In Ho Chi Minh City, according to the Ho Chi Minh City Center for Disease Control (HCDC), in week 44 (from October 26 to November 1), the city recorded 1,959 cases of dengue fever, an increase of 16.2% compared to the average of the previous four weeks. From the beginning of the year to the end of week 44, Ho Chi Minh City has recorded 44,549 cases. 17-day-old infant in severe dengue shock. Recently, the Children's Hospital of Ho Chi Minh City admitted and treated a 17-day-old boy from Tan Vinh Loc commune who suffered from dengue shock with many dangerous complications. A 17-day-old infant suffering from dengue shock is being treated at the City Children's Hospital. Photo: Provided by the hospital. Reportedly, the child's mother also had dengue fever and was treated at the Hospital for Tropical Diseases. After the mother was discharged, the child began to develop a fever. Check Symptoms According to the medical history, the child had a moderate, intermittent fever for two days, accompanied by startling during sleep and a red rash on the skin. Laboratory results showed a significant decrease in platelets, and the NS1 antigen test was positive for Dengue virus. By the third day, the child's condition worsened, exhibiting lethargy, fussiness, weak pulse, cold extremities, blood pressure dropping to 60/40 mmHg, and numerous petechiae (small hemorrhagic spots) on the skin. Laboratory tests showed a continued decrease in platelet count to 24,000/mm3, and elevated liver enzymes. Doctors diagnosed the child with dengue hemorrhagic shock, severe liver damage, and coagulation disorders. The patient received intensive shock treatment, including fluid resuscitation, blood transfusions, platelet concentrates, and albumin, while also supporting liver and respiratory function. Due to the child's young age, establishing an intravenous line proved difficult. During treatment, the child developed bruising at the injection site, vomited dark brown fluid, and exhibited unstable hemodynamics. You may also like After 72 hours of intensive treatment, the child's hemodynamic status and liver damage gradually improved, with no further signs of bleeding, and the child was alert, feeding, and urinating well. Dr. Nguyen Minh Tien, Deputy Director of the City Children's Hospital, said that dengue fever can occur in newborns, but the symptoms are sometimes atypical and easily confused with sepsis or other diseases. Check Symptoms Patients being treated for dengue fever at the Ho Chi Minh City Hospital for Tropical Diseases. Photo: DH. Check Symptoms Dengue hemorrhagic shock in this age group is uncommon and may be related to plasma leakage, myocardial failure, or sepsis. Therefore, when infants show signs of fever or other health abnormalities, families should take them to a medical facility with a neonatal specialist for examination, diagnosis of the cause, and timely treatment. The absence of fever does not mean the illness is cured. According to Dr. Nguyen Huu Tri, a specialist in the Emergency Department at Children's Hospital 2, dengue fever typically progresses through three stages: the fever stage, the critical stage, and the recovery stage. The critical stage usually occurs from the 3rd to the 7th day of the illness, especially on the 4th or 5th day, when the child's fever begins to subside or disappears. According to Dr. Nguyen Huu Tri, the period after the fever subsides is when patients are at risk of plasma leakage, leading to shock, multi-organ damage, and even death if not detected and treated promptly. Dr. Tri noted that test results need to be evaluated daily and combined with clinical manifestations. In the early days, blood counts may not change significantly, while platelet counts gradually decrease as the disease progresses. Therefore, children with dengue fever need to be closely monitored from the very first days of the illness, and should have follow-up appointments as directed by their doctor, especially during the critical phase. Not only children, but adults are also at risk of developing severe symptoms when they contract dengue fever. You may also like Dr. Nguyen Thanh Phong, Deputy Director of the Ho Chi Minh City Hospital for Tropical Diseases, said that in the last 10 years, adults have accounted for a large proportion of dengue fever cases, possibly more than two-thirds. However, many people are still complacent, believing that dengue fever is not dangerous or that the absence of fever means recovery. In reality, many patients are admitted to the hospital when they have already developed severe shock, heavy bleeding, or multiple organ failure. Dr. Nguyen Thanh Phong, a specialist in internal medicine, warns that when experiencing a high fever for three consecutive days, people should consider the possibility of dengue fever and seek medical attention for examination, testing, and appropriate treatment. In particular, if symptoms such as severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, lethargy, extreme fatigue, cold hands and feet, shortness of breath, unusual bleeding, or decreased urination appear, patients should be taken to a medical facility immediately, even if the fever has subsided. Doctors advise that people suspected of having dengue fever should stay well-hydrated, use oral rehydration solution (ORS) as directed by healthcare professionals, eat soft, easily digestible foods, and get adequate rest. They should absolutely not self-medicate with ibuprofen, aspirin, or other anti-inflammatory pain relievers due to the risk of increased bleeding. Furthermore, they should not attempt to administer intravenous fluids at home. According to the Deputy Director of the Ho Chi Minh City Hospital for Tropical Diseases, self-administering intravenous fluids when suffering from dengue fever poses many risks. Intravenous fluids administered at the wrong time or with incorrect indications can cause complications and make the process of combating shock more difficult. To prevent the disease, people need to proactively eliminate mosquitoes and larvae, remove objects that hold stagnant water, and avoid mosquito bites. supplementary_news.content: Rescuers save 17-day-old newborn boy suffering from dengue shock and severe liver damage. On the evening of November 6th, the City Children's Hospital announced that it had successfully treated a case of dengue shock in a 17-day-old infant, accompanied by severe liver damage, coagulation disorders, and severe thrombocytopenia. Check Symptoms Báo Sài Gòn Giải phóng • 06/11/2026 The child is receiving intensive treatment at the City Children's Hospital (Photo: Provided by the hospital). Discover more Find Treatments Shop Baby Gear Track Pregnancy The patient is a young boy residing in Tan Vinh Loc ward, Ho Chi Minh City, who was admitted to the hospital after two days of intermittent fever, startling awake during sleep, and a red rash on his skin. Test results showed the child was positive for the Dengue virus, and his platelet count had dropped to 47,000/mm3. By the third day of the illness, the child's condition suddenly worsened, becoming lethargic, irritable, with cold hands and feet, low blood pressure, and numerous petechiae (small hemorrhagic spots) on the skin. Tests showed a continued sharp drop in platelet count and elevated liver enzymes. Doctors diagnosed the child with dengue hemorrhagic shock, severe liver damage, and a coagulation disorder. Check Symptoms You may also like Ho Chi Minh City: Newborn baby saved from severe dengue shock. When infants show signs of fever or other health abnormalities, families should take them to a medical facility with a neonatal specialist for examination, testing, and determination of the cause. Saving the life of a newborn suffering from severe dengue shock. A 17-day-old boy with severe complications from dengue fever has been successfully treated by doctors at Ho Chi Minh City Children's Hospital. Doctors advise parents not to underestimate dengue fever, especially in children. Saving the life of a 17-day-old infant suffering from dengue shock and severe liver damage. Doctors at the Children's Hospital of Ho Chi Minh City have successfully saved a 17-day-old infant suffering from dengue shock, blood clotting disorders, and severe liver damage. The child received intensive shock treatment, including fluid resuscitation, blood transfusions, platelet concentrate, albumin, and support for liver and respiratory function. After 72 hours of treatment, hemodynamic status and liver damage improved, and the child was alert, feeding, and urinating adequately. Before the child fell ill, the mother also contracted dengue fever and was treated at the Ho Chi Minh City Hospital for Tropical Diseases. According to Dr. Nguyen Minh Tien, Deputy Director of the City Children's Hospital, dengue fever in newborns can present with atypical symptoms, easily mistaken for sepsis or other illnesses. Although dengue shock is uncommon at this age, the disease still carries the risk of serious complications. "When infants show signs of fever or other health abnormalities, families should quickly take them to a medical facility with a neonatal specialist for examination, diagnosis, and timely treatment," advised Dr. Nguyen Minh Tien. Check Symptoms You may also like 17-day-old infant suffers from dengue shock and severe liver damage. (Dan Tri Newspaper) - At just 17 days old, a baby boy in Ho Chi Minh City has fallen into a state of dengue shock, blood clotting disorder, severe liver damage, and is in critical condition. Warning of severe dengue fever in overweight children. VTV.vn - A 12-year-old boy is suffering from dengue shock accompanied by gastrointestinal bleeding, liver damage, and critical respiratory failure. Doctors warn that early recognition of severe symptoms is crucial for timely emergency treatment. A 50 kg boy is in critical condition, with liver enzymes soaring to over 3,000 U/L after 4 days of fever. After three days of high fever, the 12-year-old boy suddenly experienced abdominal pain, vomited brown fluid, had black stools, and then went into dengue shock, respiratory failure, and severe liver damage. According to the Ho Chi Minh City Center for Disease Control, from October 26th to November 1st, 2026 (week 44), the city recorded 1,959 cases of dengue fever, an increase of 16.2% compared to the average of the previous four weeks. The total number of dengue fever cases accumulated from the beginning of 2026 to week 44 is 44,549. Communes and wards with a high number of dengue fever cases per 100,000 people include Con Dao Special Zone, Ngai Giao, and Minh Thanh.
